correctness.rationale: Let r(v) be the red degree and let x(uv) indicate a red edge. The four distinct neighbouring edges must contain two red edges, i.e. r(u)+r(v)=2+2x(uv). Thus r has constant parity by connectedness. Swap the names if necessary to make it odd. Red edges then join degrees 3 and 1, blue edges join degrees 1 and 1, and the degree-3 vertices are independent and give exactly one neighbour to each remaining vertex. This recovers D and the colour uniquely. The converse satisfies the same edge equation. One colour is impossible. Disjoint closed neighbourhoods have size four; in the bipartite case equal part sizes m satisfy a+3b=m=3a+b, giving m=4a=4b. This is a symbolic proof for the full claim; the frozen checker and its reported 19-case output were inspected as supplementary evidence, not executed or used to infer the universal result.
